sections.title: Exclamation + subjunctive
sections.content: The fastest way to react is an exclamation. You know *alegría* from A2 Unit 27, as in *¡Qué alegría que vengas a la fiesta!*. The pattern is *¡Qué* + a word for the feeling + *que* + subjunctive! There is no verb of feeling: the exclamation carries the feeling, and the clause after *que* is the thing you react to.

sections.title: Common exclamations
rows: What a shame that... ! / What a pity that... !
How good that... ! (¡Qué bueno que! is very common in Latin America)
How horrible that... ! / How outrageous that... !

items.english: What a shame that you can't come!

items.spanish: ¡Qué bueno que te guste el regalo!
items.english: How good that you like the present!

items.spanish: ¡Qué bien que hayan llegado a tiempo!
items.english: How good that they have arrived on time!

items.spanish: ¡Qué barbaridad que cerraran el cine del barrio!
items.english: How outrageous that they closed the neighbourhood cinema!

sections.content: *¡Menos mal que...!* ('Thank goodness that...') is the exception. It expresses relief that something good did happen, so it takes the indicative: *¡Menos mal que llegaste a tiempo!*. Compare *¡Qué bien que hayas llegado a tiempo!*, which uses the subjunctive.
